items.followUp: Explain how a vector is represented by a directed line segment.

rubric.why: A vector’s magnitude is shown by the length of its graphical representation.
rubric.description: Represent the magnitude using the line’s length and a suitable scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the length represents magnitude, preferably in proportion to it using a scale.

rubric.why: The arrowhead distinguishes the vector’s direction.
rubric.description: Show the vector’s direction with an arrowhead.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the arrowhead as indicating direction.

modelAnswer: Represent a vector by a directed line segment, drawn to a suitable scale.
The length of the segment represents its magnitude, and its arrowhead shows its direction.

items.followUp: What is meant by the resultant of two forces acting on an object?

rubric.why: A resultant is a single force that replaces the combined forces.
rubric.description: State that the resultant is one force representing the combined forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the resultant as a single force.

rubric.why: The resultant has the same effect as all the forces acting together.
rubric.description: State that it has the same effect as the forces acting together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the equivalent effect.

modelAnswer: The resultant force is a single force that produces the same effect as two or more forces acting together.

items.followUp: Define the moment arm of a force about a pivot.

rubric.why: The moment arm is measured perpendicularly from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
rubric.description: Identify the distance as perpendicular (the shortest distance).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the distance is perpendicular or shortest.

rubric.why: The moment arm is the distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
rubric.description: Identify the two features between which the distance is measured.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the pivot and the force’s line of action.

modelAnswer: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance between the pivot and the line of action of a force.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and potential energy.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is associated with an object’s motion.
rubric.description: Define kinetic energy in terms of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that kinetic energy is the energy an object has due to its motion.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with position or configuration.
rubric.description: Define potential energy in terms of position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that potential energy is stored energy due to position or configuration.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion.
Potential energy is the stored energy an object possesses due to its position or configuration.

items.followUp: An engine receives 500 J of energy and gives 350 J of useful output energy. Find its efficiency.

rubric.why: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output to input.
rubric.description: Give the ratio used to calculate efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: Efficiency is commonly expressed as a percentage by multiplying the ratio by 100.
rubric.description: State that the ratio is multiplied by 100 to give percentage efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the percentage conversion.

modelAnswer: Alternatively, efficiency = (useful output work ÷ input work) × 100%.

items.followUp: Define density and state the density of water in SI units.

rubric.why: Density is defined as mass divided by volume.
rubric.description: Define density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The density of water is 1000 kg/m³, equivalent to 1 g/cm³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the SI value or its equivalent value.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
The density of water is 1000 kg/m³ (or 1 g/cm³).

items.followUp: What happens to an elastic object when the deforming force is removed?

rubric.why: An elastic material tends to recover its original shape and size after deformation.
rubric.description: State that the object returns to its original shape or size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the object regains its original shape or size.

rubric.why: Recovery occurs when the deforming force is removed.
rubric.description: Specify that the recovery follows removal of the deforming force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning removal of the force.

modelAnswer: Elasticity is the property of a material by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: A force of 20 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the stress.

rubric.why: Stress is the applied force divided by the area over which it acts.
rubric.description: Define stress as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of stress is the pascal, equal to one newton per square metre.
rubric.description: Give the SI unit of stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pascal (Pa) or N/m².

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².
